claims.text: The fresh catalyst is a 1 wt% multi-element alloy supported on La-doped γ-Al2O3.
The fresh catalyst initially contains agglomerates of fine metallic particles.
A high-alkalinity continuous-solvothermal synthesis at 200–350 °C is proposed.
Bayesian-driven elemental selection will enrich the catalyst in Pd, Rh, and Ga.
The optimized synthesis will reduce sintering and elemental segregation during catalyst formation.
The optimized synthesis will induce nanoscale restructuring after thermal aging.
Post-aging reconstruction will form electronically coupled Cu–Pt cooperative sites.
Maintained alloy–support interfacial states will limit phase segregation.
Maintained alloy–support interfacial states will limit detrimental Pt coordination with Ni or Fe.
Controlled multimetal nucleation and subsequent restructuring will cause beneficial electronic redistribution.
Cu–Pt cooperative sites will weaken strong CO adsorption.
Cu–Pt cooperative sites will enhance redox buffering.
Cu–Pt cooperative sites will improve oxygen mobility.
The proposed electronic and interfacial changes will improve low-temperature oxidation of CO and hydrocarbons.
The optimized catalyst will resist poisoning by H2O and NO.
The optimized catalyst will have improved durability after severe aging.
The accelerated-aging protocol is 900 °C for 5 h under cyclic lean/rich, water-containing gas, followed by oxidation/reduction treatments.
Performance is evaluated from 100 to 500 °C in a near-stoichiometric feed containing 500 ppm NO, 5000 ppm CO, 200 ppm C3H6, and 120 ppm i-C5H12.
After aging, the optimized catalyst will have a T50 at least 5 °C lower than that of the Pd/Al2O3 benchmark.
After aging, the optimized catalyst will provide at least a 2 percentage-point conversion improvement at 350 °C relative to the Pd/Al2O3 benchmark.
